rule: diameter <= largest tool diameter
note: The widest cutter of any kind the feature admits — the tightest corner (cd min) and for a hole the bore itself: past it the tool cannot finish the feature — terminal finishing rules for everything

rule: diameter <= largest tool diameter + drill oversize
note: A drill is allowed past the bore by the oversize knob: this row is the one exception to the cap above and is why raising "max drill deviation" widens the band

rule: flute length >= feature depth
note: The flutes must cover the cut or the shank rubs

rule: flute length past the corner >= feature depth + through overcut
note: A through cut runs past the bottom by the overcut — and it is the tool's corner that has to clear it
column8: so the flutes are measured below the corner (Justin Mimbs' reach-curve note)

rule: form is not flat end mill
note: A flat end cannot finish a filleted floor — terminal finishing only

rule: corner radius <= floor fillet radius
note: A bigger nose cannot sit in the fillet

rule: form in order bull nose end mill; ball end mill
note: A filleted floor wants a bull nose; a ball is usable and ranked last

rule: corner radius closest to floor fillet radius
note: Exact match first then the least under: the rule for filleted pockets

rule: corner radius <= finishing radius limit
note: A bull nose standing in for a flat end leaves a radius on a floor the model draws sharp: the engine's bullnose substitution limit

rule: corner radius <= finishing radius limit
note: Same as a pocket floor

rule: corner radius <= finishing radius limit
note: Same as a pocket floor; a wall or profile is cut by the side and its nose radius is free

rule: flute length past the corner >= feature depth + through overcut
note: A wall with nothing under it is cut clean through: the tool runs past the bottom and it is its corner that clears — the same rule as a through hole (Justin Mimbs' reach-curve note)

rule: flute length past the corner >= feature depth + through overcut
note: Same as a wall

rule: diameter <= hole diameter + drill oversize
note: The API's largest drill diameter is this with the engine's 0.001 in

rule: diameter >= hole diameter - drill undersize
note: A smaller drill is a pilot not the hole

rule: diameter <= largest end mill diameter
note: 10/11 of the hole: room to helix — the drill takes the whole bore
column8: so this limit is the end mill's alone

rule: tip angle <= tip angle + drill angle tolerance shallower
note: A 140° drill in a 118° hole leaves a shallower cone

rule: tip angle >= tip angle - drill angle tolerance sharper
note: A sharper drill leaves a step at the bottom

rule: tip angle = 180
note: A counterbore stays flat: no pointed drill ever

rule: tip angle closest to tip angle
form is drill
note: A pointed blind hole up to an inch is drilled

rule: form is drill
note: A through hole up to an inch is drilled — shop rule; a flat-bottomed hole has boring rules instead

rule: tip angle = chamfer included angle + chamfer angle tolerance
note: The tool's point angle is the whole cone: twice the bevel's angle from the axis; 0.15° in the engine

rule: flute length >= slant length
note: The cutting edge covers the bevel

rule: tip angle = chamfer included angle + chamfer angle tolerance
diameter <= entry width
note: It goes in through the opening

rule: diameter <= entry width
tip angle = taper angle + chamfer angle tolerance
tip angle = taper angle + chamfer angle tolerance
diameter <= hole diameter - thread mill margin
note: 98 % of the minor diameter

rule: furthest below holder >= depth below top
note: What stands out of the holder has to reach the bottom of the feature from the top of the part. Measured against the furthest the tool could ever stand out — its overall length less whichever holds it back first, the shank the shop keeps clamped or the share that stays in the holder — so a tool that cannot reach even pulled all the way out is not eligible. Length below holder is where the tool is set, which is shorter, and refusing on it would drop tools a shop reaches with by pulling them out

rule: form is ball end mill
note: The kernel says only a ball finishes this surface without a cusp

rule: form is not flat end mill
note: A flat end cannot finish a 3D surface: the engine's invalid finishing type — terminal finishing rules for everything

rule: form is not flat end mill
note: Same as a contour surface

rule: form is not flat end mill
note: Same as a contour surface

rule: form in order bull nose end mill; ball end mill; flat end mill
note: The engine's order for 3D: a ball has zero speed at the tip

rule: form in order bull nose end mill; ball end mill; flat end mill
form in order bull nose end mill; ball end mill; flat end mill
form in order chamfer mill; ball end mill; radius mill; flat end mill
note: The engine's order for a chamfer

rule: form in order chamfer mill; counter sink; spot drill; ball end mill
form is not ball end mill
note: The engine does not face with a ball

rule: form in order flat end mill; bull nose end mill
note: The engine's order for a wall

rule: form in order flat end mill; bull nose end mill
form in order flat end mill; bull nose end mill; ball end mill
note: A sharp floor wants a flat end

rule: form in order flat end mill; bull nose end mill; ball end mill
form in order drill; flat end mill; bull nose end mill; ball end mill
note: The engine's finish order for a hole

rule: diameter closest to hole diameter
note: An exact-size drill leads: a hole is made at its own size
column8: so nearest-to-the-bore beats the 5 %-under rule that a pocket corner wants

rule: diameter closest to largest tool diameter
note: A tool that matches the feature's own geometry exactly leads, then the nearest under it: the widest cutter the feature admits is the one that finishes it in the fewest passes

rule: L/D smallest
note: Among tools that reach — the shorter: the ideal L/D is the least that clears the holder at full depth

rule: radial clearance >= radial holder clearance
note: The holder must clear the walls sideways at the stickout it needs

rule: axial clearance >= axial holder clearance
note: The holder nose must clear the part top

rule: held share >= least hold
note: Below a quarter of the tool in the holder it is not compatible

rule: held share >= good hold
note: A quarter to a third held is possible but bad: ranked after the good ones

rule: collet series smallest
note: A smaller nose clears more
